reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited text supports it: the Agreement contains no Vendor-side audit, inspection, records-examination or verification right binding the Customer. § 6 (p0047) runs in Client's favour (documentation on request, right to contest charges), § 3(e) (p0037) gives Client — not TrueLink — access to usage statistics and logs, and § 8(f) (p0058) is platform self-help against spam/illegal activity on TrueLink's own hosted environment, not an audit of Client's usage or access to Client systems.

Correctly no redline and no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding; the rendered paragraphs are byte-identical to the originals, so no unintended or directionally wrong edit was introduced.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is properly explained as a false signal — the regex cannot match a frequency cap where no audit clause exists at all, so it does not evidence a deviation.

Silence on audit rights is more favourable to the Customer than the preferred position, so 'compliant' (rather than 'missing') is the correct classification, and the rationale sensibly flags a negotiation watch item with the preferred and fallback parameters should TrueLink later seek an audit right.
